name: The Sandstone Unmaking

detectability.signature: Massive causality inversion field with erratic temporal gradient boundaries, radiating paradox-signature tachyon bursts

proximity: Cause and effect relationships become subtly unreliable; actions occasionally precede their triggers
Ship logs develop contradictions that cannot be resolved by any crew member present
Sensor readings show objects in states they occupied hours or days prior
contact: Causality inverts locally; consequences manifest before their causes with increasing frequency
Crew members experience events in non-sequential order, losing narrative coherence of their own actions
Ship systems respond to commands before they are issued, then fail to respond when actually given
prolonged_exposure: Complete causality breakdown; the distinction between past, present, and future dissolves entirely
Physical structures begin to unbuild themselves as their assembly sequence reverses
Biological organisms experience cellular processes in reverse, with catastrophic physiological results

phenomena: Structures within the anomaly appear to erode in reverse, accreting dust and debris into increasingly ordered formations
Light within the fracture zone travels along causal rather than spatial paths, creating impossible visual geometries
Wrecked vessels inside the anomaly periodically reassemble themselves before disintegrating again in new configurations
The boundary of the anomaly resembles weathered sandstone cliffs seen from orbit, with strata of different temporal rates visible as color bands
hazards: Causality inversion can render emergency procedures counterproductive, as responses trigger before the emergencies they address
The anomaly is slowly expanding, with its boundary advancing at an estimated 0.2 kilometers per year
Navigation within the fracture is impossible; course corrections may apply to trajectories from hours in the past or future
opportunities: The reversed erosion process has assembled complex mineral formations of extraordinary scientific value
Studying the boundary dynamics offers unparalleled insight into the fundamental nature of causality
Wreckage reassembly events occasionally produce recoverable data from otherwise destroyed vessels
known_incidents: The destroyer Redoubt of Salient entered the anomaly in 2519 on a mapping mission. Its distress signal was received three days before the ship departed, and the vessel has not been recovered. Fragments of the ship periodically appear at the boundary in various states of assembly.
description: The Sandstone Unmaking is a vast, irregular region where causality has fractured beyond repair, stretching across a volume roughly 0.07 AU in radius and slowly growing. Its boundaries are visible as shimmering curtains of color-banded light, each stratum representing a different rate of temporal flow, resembling the layered cross-section of ancient sedimentary cliffs. Within, the normal sequence of cause and effect has eroded like stone under eons of wind, leaving a landscape where consequences arrive before their causes and entropy runs in whichever direction it pleases.

The anomaly's behavior is chaotic and defies prediction. Objects within the Unmaking simultaneously decay and reassemble, their histories playing out in fractured, non-linear sequences. Ships that have entered report experiences ranging from mild temporal displacement to complete narrative dissolution, where crew members could not determine the order in which their own actions occurred. The boundary advances slowly but inexorably, consuming approximately 0.2 kilometers of normal space per year, a geological pace that nonetheless alarms long-term strategic planners.

The origin and age of the Sandstone Unmaking are unknown. No natural process has been identified that could produce a causality fracture of this scale, yet no evidence of artificial origin has been found either. Some theorists propose it is a wound in spacetime left by an event that has not yet occurred, while others suggest it is the natural erosion of causal structure in a region where the substrate of reality is simply older and more worn than elsewhere. The name was coined by the first survey team, who described the experience of approaching the boundary as watching the universe forget how sandstone was made.

Current astrocartographic policy designates the Sandstone Unmaking as a Class One exclusion zone with a recommended avoidance margin of 0.15 AU beyond the visible boundary. The slow expansion is monitored by automated buoy networks that must be replaced annually as the boundary overtakes them. Despite the extreme danger, the anomaly attracts a persistent fringe of researchers, salvagers hoping to recover data from reassembled wrecks, and philosophical pilgrims drawn to a place where the arrow of time has been ground to dust.
